keyframe_review.note: German Confederation table: Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz 2,929 km2 (no year); the row's polygon is 2,551 km2 (ratio 0.87) but hides two faults. Its eastern part (12.68-13.55 E, 53.33-53.73 N, about 1,670 km2) misses the south and east of the Herrschaft Stargard: Fürstenberg, Wesenberg, Mirow, Feldberg, Woldegk and Friedland lie outside it (reviewer's point-in-polygon test), and in 1830 inside no state's shape. Six 8 km circles on those towns add six cells. Strasburg (13.74 E 53.51 N), which the reviewer also listed, is not added: the German page does not name it as part of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. Its western part (875 km2) is over-drawn against the Fürstentum Ratzeburg ('an der mecklenburgischen Westgrenze südlich von Lübeck'; a few hundred km2): the cells at 10.91/53.80 and 11.02/53.92 reach beyond Schönberg towards the Baltic coast; the pages give no boundary, so it is left, with the Lübeck circle (12 km) subtracted. Result: 15 cells (16 in the 1864-1865 shape), about 3,800 km2 on a 253 km2 cell (ratio 1.3 to 2,929 km2); the German page gives the Strelitz domanial area 1,652 km2 and the ritterschaftlich area 640 km2.

ledger.note: 1806: the map begins with the Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, set up as a duchy in its own right by the Treaty of Hamburg of 1701 ('Section 2 of the treaty established Mecklenburg-Strelitz as a duchy in its own right') with the Lordship of Stargard and the Principality of Ratzeburg; 1806 is the first year of the Cliopatria outline, not a founding. The page adds that the duchy 'was spared a French occupation in 1806 through the King of Bavaria's intervention'. The region now adds Fürstenberg, Wesenberg, Mirow, Feldberg, Woldegk and Friedland (German Mecklenburg-Strelitz page), which Cliopatria's row lacks.

1815: the duchy becomes the Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. 'In 1815, the Congress of Vienna recognized both Mecklenburg-Strelitz and Mecklenburg-Schwerin as grand duchies.' Charles joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1808 (the Confederation page: 18 February 1808) and the duchy was independent in 1813-1815.

ledger.note: November 1918: the grand duchy ends in the German Revolution. The page gives the year only (infobox 'German Revolution: 1918'; 'After World War I and the German Revolution of 1918-19 it was succeeded by the Free State of Mecklenburg-Strelitz'); the month rests on the revolution page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed' (German revolution of 1918-1919 page). Grand Duke Adolf Frederick VI had died by suicide on 23 February 1918, 'leaving his cousin Charles Michael as heir'. Infobox status 'Federal State of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

notes: REPAIR (batch eu-20-e, 2026-11-01). Every keyframe is Cliopatria's 'Free City of Lübeck' row minus a 12 km Lübeck circle, plus six 8 km circles on Fürstenberg, Mirow, Wesenberg, Feldberg, Woldegk and Friedland, the south and east of the Herrschaft Stargard that the row lacks (German Mecklenburg-Strelitz page: Neubrandenburg, Friedland, Woldegk, Strelitz, Stargard, Fürstenberg, Wesenberg, Mirow; Feldberg among the amtsfreie Städte of 1920). 15 cells, about 3,800 km2, ratio 1.3 to the 2,929 km2 of the German Confederation table. DISAGREEMENT with the reviewer: Strasburg is not added; the German page does not name it as Strelitz land. The Ratzeburg part (cells at 10.80/53.67, 10.91/53.80, 11.02/53.92, 875 km2) is over-drawn against a principality of a few hundred km2 and is left as Cliopatria has it because no page gives its boundary; the eastern cell 11.02/53.92 is probably the coast beyond Schönberg. Neustrelitz, Neubrandenburg and Stargard were already inside. The Cliopatria row is Mecklenburg-Strelitz's outline filed under the Name Free City of Lübeck (the Lübeck dossier marks it wrong); the orchestrator may prefer to rename the row. WIKIDATA: stays null, the German page shows no item id and wikidata.org is unreachable. Mecklenburg-Strelitz joined the Confederation of the Rhine on 18 February 1808; a grand duchy from 1815; a state of the German Empire in 1871. Travemünde is not drawn as Strelitz land. mecklenburg (eu-09-x) should name this dossier among its successors. Pages budget: 4 original plus 1 in the repair (German Mecklenburg-Strelitz). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (mecklenburg-strelitz_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row mecklenburg-strelitz -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. The Strelitz page gives the year 1918 only; November follows from the revolution page. Adolf Frederick VI died on 23 February 1918 and Charles Michael was his heir.
